title: Negative possession with plural owners
focus: Put the possessor first, fixed ei ole next, and the singular partitive noun last.
prerequisiteSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession

exercises.prompt: Build “You do not have a ball.” Start with the owner. Use teillä (“you as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”). Address a group.
exercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun.
requiredSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Negative possession sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.translation: You do not have a ball.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: te has the learned possession form teillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with every owner; do not change it to en, emme, or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
